rationale.conceptual: Applying standard GGA/PBE DFT to compute formation energy and band gap is a textbook methodology; the paper's results are reproduced using a common open-source library (Quantum ESPRESSO) with standard pseudopotentials. No custom algorithms or deep theoretical derivation needed beyond normal DFT practices.
rationale.execution: The pipeline requires fetching crystal structures from public databases, creating DFT input files for seven structures, running multiple geometry relaxations with convergence checks, computing formation energies from total energies, performing a band-structure calculation to determine gap type, and extracting results. This multi-step process with dependency on external tools and data sources places it at a moderate engineering level.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires standard DFT calculations (geometry relaxations and band structure) on small inorganic crystals using an open-source plane-wave code. Conceptual difficulty is low because the method is well-established and no novel algorithm is needed; execution involves multiple steps (structure fetching, input preparation, multiple relaxations, post-processing) but remains a straightforward pipeline. Resources are modest: small unit cells, CPU-only, no large data.
